  • increase injury risk.

questions.question: Explain the supercompensation theory in detail and its practical applications in periodized training programs. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the supercompensation theory in detail and its practical applications
  • in periodized training programs.?
  • Supercompensation Theory explains how the body adapts to training stress.
  • After a workout, performance temporarily decreases due to fatigue, then
  • recovers, and finally improves beyond the original level.
  • Phases of Supercompensation
  • Initial Fatigue Phase
  • Training causes muscle damage and energy depletion
  • Performance decreases
  • Recovery Phase
  • Body restores energy stores (ATP, glycogen)
  • Repairs muscle tissue
  • Supercompensation Phase
  • Performance increases above baseline
  • Ideal time for next training session
  • Involution (Reversibility) Phase
  • If no training, gains are lost
  • Graph Explanation
  • Performance ↓ (fatigue) → returns to normal → ↑ (supercompensation peak) →
  • ↓ if no training
  • Importance
  • Helps in planning training load
  • Prevents overtraining
  • Maximizes performance improvement
  • Application in Periodized Training
  • Periodization is the systematic planning of training.

questions.question: Design comprehensive plyometric programs for upper and lower body development. / [CO6]
questions.solution_html: • Design comprehensive plyometric programs for upper and lower body development. Plyometric Training involves explosive movements using the stretch-shortening cycle to improve power. Principles Warm-up is essential Quality over quantity Adequate rest between sets Progressive intensity A. Lower Body Plyometric Program Exercises Squat jumps Box jumps Bounding Depth jumps Lateral hops Program Design Frequency: 2–3 times/week Sets: 3–5 Reps: 8–12 Rest: 1–2 minutes B. Upper Body Plyometric Program Exercises Medicine ball chest pass Overhead throws Plyometric push-ups Side throws Clap push-ups Program Design Frequency: 2–3 times/week Sets: 3–4 Reps: 6–10 Rest: 1–2 minutes Safety Considerations Proper landing technique Avoid hard surfaces Suitable for trained individuals Gradual progression Benefits Improves explosive strength Enhances speed and agility Better athletic performance

questions.question: How would you apply Beep test results to improve cardiovascular endurance in athletes? / [CO7] [15x2 = 30]
questions.solution_html:
• How would you apply Beep test results to improve cardiovascular
  • endurance in athletes?
  • Beep Test (also called shuttle run test) measures aerobic endurance and
  • estimates VO₂ max.
  • Understanding Beep Test Results
  • Score = Level + Shuttle number
  • Higher level = better endurance
  • Used to assess fitness level
  • Application in Training
